name: Living room monstera

location.detail: Next to the window, 1 m from the glass

observed.watering_days_summer_note: In our house it thrives with far less water than the literature says
observed.humidity_note: Skipped misting all of last winter, zero crispy edges

general_notes:
The plant that started it all.

Came home tiny from the flower market in March 2024 and now owns the living room corner. First fenestrated leaf appeared in September 2024 — we celebrated with vermouth.

- Climbs a coco pole since spring 2025
- Leaves get wiped monthly, she repays it in shine
- **Lesson learned**: droopy leaves here mean *thirst*, not overwatering

name: Kitchen pothos

location.detail: Hanging from the shelf above the counter, out of direct sun

general_notes:
Unstoppable. Gets a trim every couple of months or she reaches the toaster.

Mother of the bedroom cutting (June 2026) — see the family line on the profile.

name: Bedroom pothos cutting

location.detail: On the dresser, morning light only

reference.source: Same care as the mother plant
reference.feeding: Not yet — too young, start next spring

general_notes:
A three-node cutting from Rapunzel, rooted in a water glass on the kitchen windowsill for a month, potted up on July 20th.

Still settling in — no watering routine established yet.

name: Bathroom calathea

location.detail: On the shelf by the frosted window — loves the shower steam

general_notes:
Earned her nickname the first week: folds up like an umbrella at the slightest offense.

- Only filtered or rain water — tap water browns the edges in days
- Survived a spider-mite scare in early July 2026 (neem oil, twice)
- Folds her leaves up every evening; it still looks like a magic trick

name: Studio snake plant

location.detail: Floor pot beside the bookshelf, afternoon light

reference.light: Anything from low light to full sun

observed.watering_days_winter_note: The studio stays cold in winter — monthly watering rotted a leaf in 2023, forty days works

general_notes:
The veteran. Predates the whole plant obsession and has survived two moves, one flooding (Pepa) and one month of total neglect (Kike).

Pups appeared in spring 2025; we still have not divided them.

name: Alocasia zebrina

location.detail: Would go on the plant stand next to the monstera

reference.feeding: Every 2–3 weeks in the growing season

general_notes:
Spotted at the little plant shop on Calle Hierbabuena — those zebra stems! Holding off until the monstera corner gets its humidifier, alocasias are famously dramatic about dry air.

Reportedly goes fully dormant in winter: do not panic, do not overwater.
